1SA.P.2.27-36.text: A Prophecy against the House of Eli

1SA.P.20.10-29.text: Jonathan and David Renew Their Covenant

1SA.P.22.1-5.text: David Flees to Adullam and Mizpeh

1SA.P.22.6-23.text: Saul Slays the Priests of Nob

1SA.P.28.7-25.text: Saul and the Medium of Endor

1SA.1.1-2.text: Elkanah has two wives, and only Peninnah has children

1SA.1.3-4.text: Elkanah goes to Shiloh each year to worship

1SA.1.5-6.text: Elkanah loves Hannah, but Peninnah taunts her

1SA.1.7-8.text: Hannah weeps, and Elkanah asks why she is sad

1SA.1.9-10.text: Hannah prays to the LORD with many tears

1SA.1.11-11.text: Hannah vows to give her son to the LORD

1SA.1.12-14.text: Eli sees Hannah praying and thinks she is drunk

1SA.1.15-16.text: Hannah tells Eli she is praying in deep grief

1SA.1.17-18.text: Eli blesses Hannah, and she leaves and eats again

1SA.1.19-20.text: The LORD gives Hannah a son, and she names him Samuel

1SA.1.21-23.text: Hannah stays home to nurse Samuel until he is weaned

1SA.1.24-25.text: Hannah brings young Samuel to Eli at Shiloh

1SA.1.26-28.text: Hannah gives Samuel to the LORD for his whole life

1SA.2.1-1.text: Hannah rejoices in the LORD’s salvation

1SA.2.2-2.text: Hannah says no one is holy like the LORD

1SA.2.3-4.text: Hannah says the LORD weighs actions and breaks the mighty

1SA.2.5-5.text: Hannah says the hungry are fed and the full must work

1SA.2.6-7.text: Hannah says the LORD controls life, death, and wealth

1SA.2.8-8.text: Hannah says the LORD lifts up the poor

1SA.2.9-9.text: Hannah says the LORD guards the faithful

1SA.2.10-10.text: Hannah says the LORD will judge and strengthen his king

1SA.2.11-11.text: Elkanah goes home, and Samuel serves the LORD under Eli

1SA.2.12-14.text: Eli’s sons are wicked and take meat from worshipers

1SA.2.15-17.text: Eli’s sons demand raw meat by force and sin greatly

1SA.2.18-19.text: Samuel serves the LORD, and Hannah brings him a robe

1SA.2.20-21.text: Eli blesses Elkanah and Hannah, and she has more children

1SA.2.22-24.text: Eli rebukes his sons for sinning at the Tent of Meeting

1SA.2.25-26.text: Eli’s sons do not listen, and Samuel keeps growing

1SA.2.27-28.text: A man of God tells Eli how the LORD chose Eli’s family

1SA.2.29-30.text: God says Eli honored his sons more than the LORD

1SA.2.31-33.text: The LORD says Eli’s family will lose strength and die

1SA.2.34-35.text: Hophni and Phinehas will die on the same day

1SA.2.36-36.text: Eli’s family will beg for food and priestly work

1SA.3.1-4.text: The LORD calls Samuel while he lies in the temple

1SA.3.5-6.text: Samuel runs to Eli twice, but Eli did not call him

1SA.3.7-8.text: The LORD calls a third time, and Eli understands

1SA.3.9-9.text: Eli tells Samuel how to answer the LORD

1SA.3.10-11.text: The LORD calls Samuel and says he will act in Israel

1SA.3.12-14.text: The LORD tells Samuel he will judge Eli’s family

1SA.3.15-16.text: Samuel is afraid to tell Eli about the vision

1SA.3.17-18.text: Samuel tells Eli everything the LORD said

1SA.3.19-21.text: All Israel knows that Samuel is the LORD’s prophet

1SA.4.1-2.text: The Philistines defeat Israel in battle at Aphek

1SA.4.3-4.text: The elders of Israel bring the ark from Shiloh

1SA.4.5-6.text: Israel shouts when the ark comes, and the Philistines hear

1SA.4.7-9.text: The Philistines are afraid but urge each other to fight

1SA.4.10-11.text: Israel loses the battle, and the ark is captured

1SA.4.12-13.text: A man from Benjamin brings bad news to Shiloh

1SA.4.14-15.text: Eli hears the outcry and asks what has happened

1SA.4.16-17.text: The messenger tells Eli that his sons are dead

1SA.4.18-18.text: Eli falls from his chair and dies

1SA.4.19-20.text: Phinehas’s wife gives birth and dies after the bad news

1SA.4.21-22.text: The woman names her son Ichabod because glory has gone

1SA.5.1-3.text: The Philistines put the ark beside Dagon, and Dagon falls

1SA.5.4-5.text: Dagon falls again, and his head and hands break off

1SA.5.6-7.text: The LORD sends tumors on Ashdod, and the people want the ark gone

1SA.5.8-9.text: The Philistines move the ark to Gath, and sickness follows

1SA.5.10-10.text: The people of Ekron cry out when the ark arrives

1SA.5.11-12.text: The Ekronites ask the rulers to send the ark away

1SA.6.1-2.text: The Philistines ask their priests how to send the ark back

1SA.6.3-4.text: The priests tell the Philistines to send gold offerings

1SA.6.5-6.text: The priests urge the Philistines to honor Israel’s God

1SA.6.7-9.text: The priests give a plan to send the ark on a cart

1SA.6.10-12.text: The cows pull the ark straight toward Beth-shemesh

1SA.6.13-13.text: The people of Beth-shemesh are glad to see the ark

1SA.6.14-15.text: Beth-shemesh offers the cows and sacrifices to the LORD

1SA.6.16-16.text: The Philistine rulers see this and return to Ekron

1SA.6.17-18.text: The gold offerings match the five Philistine cities

1SA.6.19-20.text: God strikes men of Beth-shemesh who looked in the ark

1SA.6.21-21.text: The men of Beth-shemesh ask Kiriath-jearim to take the ark

1SA.7.1-2.text: Men of Kiriath-jearim keep the ark for twenty years

1SA.7.3-4.text: Samuel tells Israel to put away foreign gods

1SA.7.5-6.text: Israel gathers at Mizpah and confesses sin

1SA.7.7-8.text: Israel fears the Philistines and asks Samuel to pray

1SA.7.9-9.text: Samuel offers a lamb and God answers his prayer

1SA.7.10-11.text: God thunders and the Philistines flee from Israel

1SA.7.12-12.text: Samuel sets up a stone named Ebenezer

1SA.7.13-14.text: The Philistines are subdued and Israel gets its cities back

1SA.7.15-17.text: Samuel judges Israel all his life

1SA.8.4-5.text: Israel’s elders ask Samuel for a king

1SA.8.6-7.text: God tells Samuel Israel has rejected God as king

1SA.8.8-9.text: God tells Samuel to warn the people about a king

1SA.8.10-12.text: Samuel warns that a king will take sons for war

1SA.8.13-15.text: Samuel warns that the king will take daughters and fields

1SA.8.16-18.text: Samuel warns that the people will become the king’s slaves

1SA.8.19-20.text: The people refuse to listen and demand a king

1SA.8.21-22.text: God tells Samuel to give the people a king

1SA.9.1-2.text: Kish has a son named Saul, tall and handsome

1SA.9.3-4.text: Saul and a servant look for Kish’s lost donkeys

1SA.9.5-6.text: Saul’s servant suggests asking the man of God

1SA.9.7-8.text: Saul and the servant plan a gift for the man of God

1SA.9.9-11.text: Saul and the servant ask young women about the seer

1SA.9.12-13.text: Young women tell Saul to hurry to find the seer

1SA.9.14-14.text: Saul meets Samuel at the city entrance

1SA.9.15-16.text: God tells Samuel to anoint the man from Benjamin

1SA.9.17-19.text: God shows Samuel the man who will rule Israel

1SA.9.20-21.text: Saul says his clan is too small for such honor

1SA.9.22-22.text: Samuel seats Saul in the place of honor

1SA.9.23-24.text: Samuel gives Saul the special portion of meat

1SA.9.25-26.text: Samuel talks with Saul on the roof at dawn

1SA.9.27-27.text: Samuel tells Saul to stay and hear God’s word

1SA.10.1-2.text: Samuel anoints Saul as ruler over Israel

1SA.10.3-4.text: Samuel tells Saul about three men he will meet

1SA.10.5-6.text: Samuel says the Spirit will change Saul among prophets

1SA.10.7-8.text: Samuel tells Saul to wait seven days at Gilgal

1SA.10.9-10.text: God changes Saul’s heart and the signs come true

1SA.10.11-13.text: People are surprised to see Saul among the prophets

1SA.10.14-16.text: Saul does not tell his uncle about the kingship

1SA.10.17-19.text: Samuel says Israel rejected God by wanting a king

1SA.10.20-21.text: Saul is selected but cannot be found

1SA.10.22-23.text: Saul is found hiding and stands taller than all

1SA.10.24-24.text: The people shout for Saul as the king the LORD chose

1SA.10.25-25.text: Samuel explains the rights of kingship to the people

1SA.10.26-27.text: Saul goes home, but some men despise him

1SA.11.1-2.text: Nahash threatens to put out everyone’s right eye

1SA.11.3-3.text: Jabesh’s elders ask for seven days to find help

1SA.11.4-5.text: The people weep, and Saul asks what is wrong

1SA.11.6-8.text: Saul calls Israel to war and many men come

1SA.11.9-10.text: Saul promises the men of Jabesh help by tomorrow

1SA.11.11-11.text: Saul’s three divisions attack and scatter the Ammonites

1SA.11.12-13.text: Saul forbids killing anyone, for the LORD saved Israel

1SA.11.14-15.text: Samuel and the people confirm Saul as king at Gilgal

1SA.12.1-2.text: Samuel says he has led Israel since his youth

1SA.12.3-3.text: Samuel asks Israel to say if he has wronged anyone

1SA.12.4-5.text: Israel agrees that Samuel has never wronged anyone

1SA.12.6-7.text: Samuel says the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt

1SA.12.8-9.text: Israel’s fathers forgot the LORD and faced enemies

1SA.12.10-11.text: The LORD sends leaders to save Israel from enemies

1SA.12.12-13.text: Samuel says Israel chose a king, though the LORD was king

1SA.12.14-15.text: Samuel tells Israel to follow the LORD and not rebel

1SA.12.16-18.text: The LORD sends thunder and rain at Samuel’s call

1SA.12.19-21.text: Samuel tells Israel to serve the LORD, not worthless things

1SA.12.22-23.text: Samuel promises to keep praying for Israel and teaching

1SA.12.24-25.text: Samuel urges Israel to fear the LORD and serve him

1SA.13.1-2.text: Saul becomes king and chooses three thousand men

1SA.13.3-4.text: Jonathan attacks the Philistines and Saul calls Israel

1SA.13.5-5.text: The Philistines gather a huge army at Michmash

1SA.13.6-7.text: The men of Israel hide in fear while Saul stays at Gilgal

1SA.13.8-10.text: Saul offers the sacrifice when Samuel does not come

1SA.13.11-12.text: Saul tells Samuel why he offered the sacrifice

1SA.13.13-14.text: Samuel tells Saul his kingdom will not last

1SA.13.15-15.text: Samuel leaves Gilgal and Saul counts six hundred men

1SA.13.16-16.text: Saul and Jonathan stay at Geba near the Philistines

1SA.13.17-18.text: Philistine raiders go out in three groups

1SA.13.19-21.text: The Philistines let no blacksmith work in Israel

1SA.13.22-23.text: Only Saul and Jonathan have weapons on the day of battle

1SA.14.1-1.text: Jonathan decides to attack the Philistine outpost

1SA.14.2-3.text: Saul waits at Migron with about six hundred men

1SA.14.4-5.text: Two cliffs stand beside the pass Jonathan will cross

1SA.14.6-7.text: Jonathan trusts the LORD, and his armor-bearer agrees

1SA.14.8-10.text: Jonathan sets a sign to know the LORD will help

1SA.14.11-12.text: Philistine guards call Jonathan and his armor-bearer up

1SA.14.13-14.text: Jonathan and his armor-bearer kill about twenty men

1SA.14.15-15.text: God causes great fear among the Philistines

1SA.14.16-17.text: Saul learns that Jonathan and his armor-bearer are gone

1SA.14.18-19.text: Saul asks Ahijah for the ark, then stops him

1SA.14.20-21.text: Saul’s army finds the Philistines fighting each other

1SA.14.22-23.text: The LORD saves Israel as more men join the battle

1SA.14.24-26.text: Saul forbids the troops to eat before evening

1SA.14.27-28.text: Jonathan eats honey without knowing Saul’s oath

1SA.14.29-30.text: Jonathan says Saul’s oath harmed the people

1SA.14.31-32.text: Hungry troops eat meat with the blood still in it

1SA.14.33-34.text: Saul has the troops slaughter animals at a large stone

1SA.14.35-35.text: Saul builds his first altar to the LORD

1SA.14.36-36.text: Saul plans a night attack, but the priest says ask God

1SA.14.37-37.text: Saul asks God about attacking, but God does not answer

1SA.14.38-39.text: Saul swears to kill whoever sinned, even Jonathan

1SA.14.40-42.text: Saul casts lots and Jonathan is chosen

1SA.14.43-44.text: Jonathan admits eating honey; Saul says he must die

1SA.14.45-46.text: The people refuse to let Saul kill Jonathan

1SA.14.47-48.text: Saul fights and defeats Israel’s enemies on every side

1SA.14.49-51.text: Saul’s family and the commander of his army

1SA.14.52-52.text: Saul enlists strong and brave men for the war

1SA.15.1-3.text: Samuel tells Saul to destroy the Amalekites

1SA.15.4-5.text: Saul gathers an army and goes to Amalek’s city

1SA.15.6-7.text: Saul warns the Kenites, then defeats the Amalekites

1SA.15.8-9.text: Saul spares King Agag and the best animals

1SA.15.10-11.text: God regrets making Saul king, and Samuel is distressed

1SA.15.12-13.text: Samuel finds Saul, who says he obeyed the LORD

1SA.15.14-16.text: Saul says the animals were kept for sacrifice

1SA.15.17-19.text: Samuel asks Saul why he did not obey the LORD

1SA.15.20-21.text: Saul says he obeyed and blames the troops

1SA.15.22-23.text: Samuel says obeying God is better than sacrifice

1SA.15.24-25.text: Saul admits his sin and asks Samuel to return with him

1SA.15.26-27.text: Samuel refuses to go back with Saul; the robe tears

1SA.15.28-29.text: Samuel says God has torn the kingdom from Saul

1SA.15.30-31.text: Saul asks for honor, and Samuel goes back with him

1SA.15.32-33.text: Samuel kills Agag king of the Amalekites

1SA.15.34-35.text: Samuel and Saul part, and Samuel mourns for Saul

1SA.16.1-1.text: The LORD sends Samuel to Bethlehem to find a king

1SA.16.2-3.text: Samuel fears Saul, but the LORD gives a plan

1SA.16.4-5.text: Samuel goes to Bethlehem and invites Jesse’s family

1SA.16.6-7.text: The LORD looks at the heart, so Eliab is not chosen

1SA.16.8-10.text: Jesse presents seven sons, but the LORD chooses none

1SA.16.11-12.text: Jesse sends for David, and the LORD chooses him

1SA.16.13-13.text: Samuel anoints David, and the LORD’s Spirit comes on him

1SA.16.14-16.text: Saul’s servants suggest a harp player to ease his distress

1SA.16.17-19.text: Saul asks for a harp player and sends for David

1SA.16.20-21.text: David comes to Saul and becomes his armor-bearer

1SA.16.22-23.text: Saul keeps David, whose harp makes Saul well

1SA.17.1-1.text: The Philistines gather for war at Socoh in Judah

1SA.17.2-3.text: Israel and the Philistines face each other in the valley

1SA.17.4-5.text: Goliath, the Philistine champion, wears heavy bronze armor

1SA.17.6-7.text: Goliath carries a bronze javelin and a heavy spear

1SA.17.8-9.text: Goliath tells Israel to send one man to fight him

1SA.17.10-11.text: Goliath defies Israel, and Saul and Israel are afraid

1SA.17.12-13.text: David’s father Jesse has eight sons; three follow Saul

1SA.17.14-16.text: David tends sheep while Goliath comes out for forty days

1SA.17.17-18.text: Jesse sends David with food to his brothers at the camp

1SA.17.19-21.text: David leaves the sheep and reaches the army camp

1SA.17.22-24.text: David greets his brothers, and Israel flees from Goliath

1SA.17.25-25.text: Israel’s men tell of the king’s reward for killing Goliath

1SA.17.26-27.text: David asks what the reward is for killing the Philistine

1SA.17.28-30.text: Eliab angrily questions why David has come to the battle

1SA.17.31-33.text: David offers to fight Goliath, but Saul doubts

1SA.17.34-35.text: David tells Saul how he saved sheep from lions and bears

1SA.17.36-36.text: David says Goliath will be like the lions and bears

1SA.17.37-37.text: David trusts the LORD, and Saul lets David go

1SA.17.38-38.text: Saul dresses David in Saul’s own armor

1SA.17.39-40.text: David removes the armor and goes out with sling and stones

1SA.17.41-43.text: Goliath despises David and curses David by his gods

1SA.17.44-45.text: Goliath threatens David; David comes in the LORD’s name

1SA.17.46-47.text: David says the LORD will give victory over the Philistines

1SA.17.48-49.text: David hits Goliath with a stone, and Goliath falls

1SA.17.50-51.text: David kills Goliath, and the Philistines run away

1SA.17.52-54.text: Israel chases the Philistines and plunders the camps

1SA.17.55-56.text: Saul asks Abner whose son David is

1SA.17.57-58.text: Abner brings David to Saul, and David names Jesse

1SA.18.1-2.text: Jonathan loves David, and Saul keeps David close

1SA.18.3-4.text: Jonathan makes a covenant with David and gives gifts

1SA.18.5-5.text: David succeeds and Saul puts David over the men of war

1SA.18.6-7.text: Israel’s women sing that David killed more than Saul

1SA.18.8-9.text: Saul is angry about the song and is jealous of David

1SA.18.10-12.text: Saul throws a spear at David and fears him

1SA.18.13-14.text: Saul gives David command of a thousand men

1SA.18.15-16.text: Saul fears David, but Israel and Judah love him

1SA.18.17-18.text: Saul offers Merab to David, hoping Philistines kill David

1SA.18.19-19.text: Saul gives Merab to Adriel instead of David

1SA.18.20-21.text: Michal loves David, and Saul plans to use her as a trap

1SA.18.22-22.text: Saul sends his servants to speak privately to David

1SA.18.23-24.text: David says he is too poor to be the king’s son-in-law

1SA.18.25-26.text: Saul asks David for a hundred Philistine foreskins

1SA.18.27-29.text: David kills two hundred Philistines and marries Michal

1SA.18.30-30.text: David is more successful than all Saul’s officers

1SA.19.1-3.text: Saul orders David killed, but Jonathan warns David

1SA.19.4-5.text: Jonathan defends David to his father Saul

1SA.19.6-7.text: Saul promises not to kill David, and David returns

1SA.19.8-9.text: David defeats the Philistines, and Saul is troubled again

1SA.19.10-11.text: Saul tries to spear David, and Michal warns David

1SA.19.12-13.text: Michal helps David escape and puts an idol in his bed

1SA.19.14-15.text: Michal tells Saul’s messengers that David is ill

1SA.19.16-17.text: Saul finds the idol, and Michal says David threatened her

1SA.19.18-20.text: David goes to Samuel, and Saul’s messengers prophesy

1SA.19.21-22.text: More messengers prophesy, so Saul goes to Ramah himself

1SA.19.23-24.text: The Spirit of God comes on Saul, and he prophesies

1SA.20.1-2.text: David asks Jonathan why Saul wants to kill him

1SA.20.3-3.text: David tells Jonathan he is close to death

1SA.20.4-5.text: Jonathan offers to help, and David plans to hide

1SA.20.6-7.text: David tells Jonathan what to say to Saul

1SA.20.8-9.text: David asks Jonathan to be faithful, and Jonathan agrees

1SA.20.10-11.text: David and Jonathan go out into the field

1SA.20.12-13.text: Jonathan swears to send David away safely

1SA.20.14-16.text: Jonathan asks David to be kind to his family always

1SA.20.17-19.text: Jonathan tells David where to hide for three days

1SA.20.20-21.text: Jonathan plans to use arrows to signal David

1SA.20.22-23.text: Jonathan tells David how he will signal danger

1SA.20.24-25.text: Saul sits to eat and David’s place is empty

1SA.20.26-27.text: Saul asks why David has not come to the meal

1SA.20.28-29.text: Jonathan tells Saul that David went to Bethlehem

1SA.20.30-31.text: Saul angrily tells Jonathan that David must die

1SA.20.32-34.text: Saul throws his spear at Jonathan, who leaves in anger

1SA.20.35-37.text: Jonathan shoots arrows beyond a boy as a signal

1SA.20.38-40.text: Jonathan sends the boy back to the city

1SA.20.41-42.text: David and Jonathan weep and say goodbye

1SA.21.1-2.text: David tells Ahimelech he is on a secret mission

1SA.21.3-4.text: David asks for bread; Ahimelech has only holy bread

1SA.21.5-6.text: Ahimelech gives David the consecrated bread

1SA.21.7-7.text: Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s servant, is at Nob

1SA.21.8-9.text: David asks for a sword and takes Goliath’s sword

1SA.21.10-11.text: David flees to Gath, where Achish’s servants know him

1SA.21.12-13.text: David is afraid and acts like a madman

1SA.22.1-2.text: David hides in the cave and men gather around him

1SA.22.3-5.text: David leaves his parents with Moab’s king and goes to Judah

1SA.22.6-6.text: Saul learns that David has been found

1SA.22.7-8.text: Saul accuses his servants of conspiring with David

1SA.22.9-10.text: Doeg tells Saul that Ahimelech helped David

1SA.22.11-13.text: Saul calls the priests and accuses Ahimelech

1SA.22.14-15.text: Ahimelech defends David and says he knew nothing

1SA.22.16-17.text: Saul orders the priests killed, but his guards refuse

1SA.22.18-19.text: Doeg kills the priests and the people of Nob

1SA.22.20-21.text: Abiathar escapes and tells David about the priests

1SA.22.22-23.text: David promises to keep Abiathar safe

1SA.23.1-2.text: God tells David to attack the Philistines at Keilah

1SA.23.3-4.text: David’s men are afraid, but God promises victory

1SA.23.5-6.text: David defeats the Philistines and saves Keilah

1SA.23.7-9.text: Saul plans to trap David at Keilah

1SA.23.10-11.text: David asks God if Saul will come to Keilah

1SA.23.12-12.text: The LORD tells David that Keilah will surrender him

1SA.23.13-14.text: David leaves Keilah and Saul cannot catch him

1SA.23.15-16.text: Jonathan visits David and strengthens his trust in God

1SA.23.17-18.text: Jonathan and David make a covenant before the LORD

1SA.23.19-20.text: The Ziphites tell Saul where David is hiding

1SA.23.21-23.text: Saul asks the Ziphites to find David’s hiding places

1SA.23.24-25.text: David goes to the Wilderness of Maon, and Saul follows

1SA.23.26-27.text: A messenger calls Saul away as he closes in on David

1SA.23.28-29.text: Saul stops chasing David, and David goes to En-gedi

1SA.24.1-2.text: Saul takes three thousand men to look for David

1SA.24.3-4.text: David cuts off a corner of Saul’s robe in the cave

1SA.24.5-7.text: David feels guilty and stops his men from killing Saul

1SA.24.8-9.text: David calls to Saul and bows before him

1SA.24.10-11.text: David says he spared Saul’s life in the cave

1SA.24.12-13.text: David asks the LORD to judge between him and Saul

1SA.24.14-15.text: David asks why Saul chases a dead dog or a flea

1SA.24.16-16.text: Saul weeps when he hears David’s voice

1SA.24.17-18.text: Saul admits David has been good to him

1SA.24.19-20.text: Saul says David will be king of Israel

1SA.24.21-22.text: David swears not to wipe out Saul’s descendants

1SA.25.2-3.text: Nabal is rich and harsh, and his wife Abigail is wise

1SA.25.4-6.text: David sends ten young men to greet Nabal

1SA.25.7-8.text: David asks Nabal for food, saying his men did no harm

1SA.25.9-11.text: Nabal refuses to give anything to David’s men

1SA.25.12-13.text: David orders his men to put on swords

1SA.25.14-15.text: A servant tells Abigail that David’s men were kind

1SA.25.16-17.text: The servant warns Abigail of disaster for Nabal’s house

1SA.25.18-19.text: Abigail secretly takes food to meet David

1SA.25.20-20.text: Abigail meets David and his men in a ravine

1SA.25.21-22.text: David swears to kill all of Nabal’s men

1SA.25.23-24.text: Abigail bows before David and asks to speak

1SA.25.25-26.text: Abigail asks David to ignore Nabal, who is a fool

1SA.25.27-28.text: Abigail gives David a gift and asks his forgiveness

1SA.25.29-29.text: Abigail says the LORD will protect David’s life

1SA.25.30-31.text: Abigail asks David to remember her when he is king

1SA.25.32-33.text: David thanks God and Abigail for stopping his revenge

1SA.25.34-35.text: David accepts Abigail’s gift and sends her home in peace

1SA.25.36-36.text: Abigail finds Nabal drunk at his feast

1SA.25.37-38.text: Nabal becomes like a stone and the LORD strikes him dead

1SA.25.39-40.text: David praises the LORD and asks Abigail to marry him

1SA.25.41-42.text: Abigail goes with David’s servants and becomes his wife

1SA.25.43-44.text: David has two wives; Saul gives Michal to Palti

1SA.26.1-2.text: The Ziphites tell Saul where David is hiding

1SA.26.3-4.text: Saul camps near David, and David sends spies

1SA.26.5-5.text: David sees where Saul and Abner are sleeping

1SA.26.6-8.text: Abishai wants to kill sleeping Saul with the spear

1SA.26.9-10.text: David tells Abishai not to kill Saul

1SA.26.11-12.text: David takes Saul’s spear and water jug and leaves

1SA.26.13-14.text: David calls out to Abner from the mountain

1SA.26.15-16.text: David accuses Abner of not protecting the king

1SA.26.17-18.text: Saul knows David’s voice; David asks why Saul chases him

1SA.26.19-20.text: David asks Saul to stop hunting him

1SA.26.21-21.text: Saul admits his sin and asks David to come back

1SA.26.22-23.text: David returns the spear and trusts the LORD to repay

1SA.26.24-25.text: David asks the LORD to value his life; Saul blesses him

1SA.27.1-1.text: David decides to escape to the land of the Philistines

1SA.27.2-4.text: David and his men live in Gath, and Saul stops searching

1SA.27.5-7.text: Achish gives David the town of Ziklag

1SA.27.8-9.text: David raids the Geshurites, Girzites and Amalekites

1SA.27.10-10.text: David tells Achish he raided places in Judah

1SA.27.11-12.text: Achish trusts David, who leaves no one alive

1SA.28.1-2.text: Achish says David and his men must fight Israel

1SA.28.3-4.text: Philistines camp at Shunem and Saul at Gilboa

1SA.28.5-6.text: Saul is afraid, and the LORD does not answer him

1SA.28.7-7.text: Saul’s servants tell him of a medium at Endor

1SA.28.8-10.text: Saul disguises himself and asks the medium for a spirit

1SA.28.11-12.text: Saul asks the medium to bring up Samuel

1SA.28.13-14.text: The woman sees Samuel, and Saul bows down

1SA.28.15-15.text: Saul tells Samuel that God no longer answers him

1SA.28.16-17.text: Samuel says the LORD has given the kingdom to David

1SA.28.18-19.text: Samuel says Saul and his sons will die tomorrow

1SA.28.20-21.text: Saul falls down in fear, weak from not eating

1SA.28.22-23.text: The woman and servants urge Saul to eat

1SA.28.24-25.text: The woman cooks a meal for Saul and his servants

1SA.29.1-2.text: The Philistines gather, and David marches with Achish

1SA.29.3-3.text: Achish defends David to the Philistine commanders

1SA.29.4-4.text: The commanders tell Achish to send David back

1SA.29.5-5.text: The commanders remind Achish of the song about David

1SA.29.6-7.text: Achish tells David to go home in peace

1SA.29.8-9.text: David asks why he cannot go to battle with Achish

1SA.29.10-11.text: David and his men go back early in the morning

1SA.30.1-2.text: The Amalekites burn Ziklag and take the people captive

1SA.30.3-4.text: David and his men find Ziklag burned and weep

1SA.30.5-6.text: David is greatly distressed but finds strength in the LORD

1SA.30.7-8.text: The LORD tells David to pursue the raiders

1SA.30.9-10.text: David leaves two hundred tired men at Besor

1SA.30.11-12.text: David’s men find and feed a starving Egyptian

1SA.30.13-14.text: The Egyptian says he was a slave of an Amalekite

1SA.30.15-15.text: The Egyptian promises to lead David to the raiders

1SA.30.16-17.text: David defeats the Amalekites; four hundred escape

1SA.30.18-20.text: David recovers everything the Amalekites had taken

1SA.30.21-22.text: Wicked men refuse to share plunder with the tired men

1SA.30.23-25.text: David says all the men will share the plunder alike

1SA.30.26-28.text: David sends plunder to the elders of Judah

1SA.30.29-31.text: David sends gifts to friends in more towns

1SA.31.1-3.text: The Philistines defeat Israel and kill Saul’s sons

1SA.31.4-6.text: Saul and his armor-bearer kill themselves

1SA.31.7-8.text: Israelites flee, and the Philistines take the towns

1SA.31.9-10.text: The Philistines hang Saul’s body at Beth-shan
